To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the retrograde atrial activation sequence during right ventricular extrastimulation is dependent on the coupling interval of the extrastimulus.

1) the ventriculoatrium interval is prolonged during right ventricular extrastimulation in concealed left-sided accessory pathway patients; 2) the ventriculoutricular interval is prolonged at long coupling intervals in all patients; 3) the ventricularoutricular interval remains unchanged at short coupling intervals when the accessory pathway conducts; and 4) the ventricuoutricular interval shortens when the atrioventicular node conducts at short coupling intervals.

(1) the ventricle-to-right atrial interval prolongs with increasing prematurity of ventricular extrastimulation in the setting of concealed left-sided Kent pathway, (2) the ventrictor left atrial interval remains constant until the refractoriness of the accessory pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of ventriculo-atrial conduction during right ventricular stimulation in patients with a concealed left-sided Kent pathway.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ventricle-to-left atrial interval is constant until the refractoriness of the accessory pathway is reached and that the ventrictle-to-right atrial interval is prolonged by the refractoriness or conduction delay in the accessory pathway.
in patients with left sided concealed accessory pathways, ventricular pacing can be used safely for the induction of tachycardias and the study of retrograde conduction.
in the absence of an accessory pathway, ventricular pacing should not produce left atrial activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

retrograde atrial activation during ventricular extrastimulation is not a reliable indicator of the presence of a concealed accessory pathway and that the presence of an accessory pathway may be suspected if the ventriculoatria interval is prolonged in the absence of an intraventricular conduction defect.
in patients with concealed Kent pathways the accessory pathway is not the sole pathway of ventriculo atrial conduction.

retrograde conduction during right ventricular extrastimulation in patients with concealed accessory pathways is usually via the accessory pathway, but that the ventriculo-atrial interval may prolong as a result of atrioventricular nodal delay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the left atrium should be included in the electrophysiological study of concealed accessory pathways.
